expected_findings.description: The docstring says a produce still in flight "holds the batch" without saying what holding does: the batch could be kept in memory, blocked from the next step, or held back from committing offsets. The same file's previous comment said it in full ("holds the batch's offset commit until the produce lands", visible as a removed line in this diff), and the only pre-existing uses elsewhere are "holds the batch lock" and "holds the batch in flight", which are different things. The fix is to write the behavior: the batch does not commit its offsets until the broker answers.

"Each host disposes of a rejected side effect differently" names a behavior the very next clause already spells out (consumer-v2 latches a fatal and holds the offset, consumer-v1 stops the process, ingestion-api-server stops the pod). The label is redundant rather than unresolvable, so the fix is to delete it and let the list carry the sentence, or to state the shared consequence directly: only one host redelivers the batch, the rest stop the process or the pod.

"The contract now sits on PipelineContext.sideEffects" gives "the contract" no antecedent: a reader has to guess which rule moved. The fix is to say what the referenced type now states, for example that PipelineContext.sideEffects says a side effect must not reject and lists what each host does with one.

false_positive_traps.description: "In flight" appears 88 times in nodejs/src before this PR and reads the same way to any engineer. It sits in the same sentence as the "holds the batch" finding, so a check that flags the sentence wholesale rather than the coined half is wrong.
"Load-bearing" has 10 pre-existing uses across unrelated modules, all meaning the same thing. Rewriting it makes the diff noisier without making it clearer.

The hardest trap: "holds the offset" uses the same verb as the flagged "holds the batch" and must not fire. "The offset" names the thing that changes state, so the phrase resolves on its own. The human reviewer kept this one and rewrote the other.
"Latches a fatal" is anchored to consumer-v2.ts's own `fatalError` and to 10 pre-existing uses of latch/latched in the consumer and pipeline code.
"Drained with the batch" uses drain/drained, which has 82 pre-existing uses in nodejs/src.
"Best effort" is added by this PR but has 36 pre-existing uses in nodejs/src and is ordinary software English besides.
